notes: The public visa-class field is an exact target for the HKB's value-domain illustration.
The public LCA flag exactly stores the status; workforce counts needed to reconstruct the legal thresholds are not asserted.
The public LCA flag exactly stores the designation described by the HKB.
The public LCA boolean is the exact field illustrated by the full-time definition.
The LCA wage-level field is an exact single-field target for the four-level domain explanation.
The HKB gives illustrative NAICS values for the exact public NAICS-code field.
The HKB gives illustrative SOC values for the exact public SOC-code field.
The structured prevailing-wage unit leaf exactly carries the Hour, Week, Month, and Year domain described by the HKB.
Representation is stored on case-attorney rows, while absence is defined by whether a case has any qualifying row; existence and multiple-attorney behavior are unspecified.
The public-disclosure field is the exact target for this open-ended option illustration.
Both exact annual-USD inputs exist on the same LCA row, so no unit conversion or relationship is required.
Both dates are TEXT and the public metadata shows different formats; no exact parsing rule is declared.
Approval rate requires certified and total counts at a target reporting grain, which the HKB does not choose.
A case load is a count across case-attorney rows and requires a defined attorney grain and deduplication rule.
Employer and global H-1B application counts require aggregation and a reporting population.
Worker-position and worksite counts coexist at the application row grain and directly support the declared ratio.
The HKB says minimum required wage may be prevailing wage or a higher regulatory amount, but no exact selection rule or field is declared.
Certified and total case counts must be aggregated to employer grain.
State is stored at worksite grain, while the numerator and denominator require application counts and a case-worksite relationship policy.
Industry and total application counts require aggregation over a defined LCA population.
Counts per SOC and the average across SOC groups are aggregate quantities with an unspecified reporting population.
An exact offered wage exists, but no public cost-of-living-index field exists.
Monthly counts and their average require temporal aggregation, and the receipt date is unparsed TEXT.
Attorney assignment and case status are on different tables; approval counting and multi-attorney attribution are unspecified.
Continuation positions are recorded per case, but an employer-level application-rate numerator and denominator require aggregation semantics.
The rate requires case-level attorney existence, deduplication of multiple attorney rows, and a total-case denominator.
The diversity sum requires allocating workers from cases to individual worksites and aggregating at employer grain.
Employer and industry average wages require two aggregation grains and a defined comparison population.
Visa-class and total application counts require aggregation over a defined application population.
Employer counts and the average count across employers require two aggregate grains.
The dependency is same-row on each LCA, but the requested result is an average across applications grouped by industry.
The numerator requires an average across parsed processing times, while H12 is blocked by undeclared date parsing.
The concentration sum inherits state-distribution aggregation and unresolved case-to-worksite allocation.
Distinct visa types per attorney require joining attorney assignments to cases and defining the total visa-type domain.
The industry concentration sum requires industry-level shares across an application population.
Current- and previous-year averages require temporal grouping, a similar-position grain, and year-boundary rules.
The factors exist on case rows, but the weights and binary conversion rules are not declared, and H2/H3 are contextual rather than compiled dependencies.
Neither worksite nor national cost-of-living index exists in the public schema, and H22 is unsupported for the same reason.
The rate requires aggregating timeline rows to a case population; H12 processing duration is declared but not used by the formula.
The exact greater-than-20-percent threshold composes the same-row compiled WDR dependency.
Both dates are heterogeneous TEXT and the month-based category boundaries do not specify exact interval or partial-month behavior.
Visa applications can be grouped by industry, but total industry workforce is absent and the industry reporting grain is unresolved.
WDR is available per LCA, but a statistically significant application count by occupation is an unspecified aggregate rule.
Location exists at worksite grain, but application allocation, national-average comparison, and population data are unresolved or absent.
Attorney visa-type distributions require a join and aggregation; even-distribution and significant-experience rules are not quantified.
Annual employer application counts require parsing receipt dates, choosing year boundaries, and aggregating cases.
The exact application-status field is enriched with the HKB outcome vocabulary, which is broader than the schema metadata's listed certified variants.
The declared closed thresholds compile directly from same-row WDR.
Wage level is only a stated correlation; experience requirements and exact rules for the three categories are absent.
Seasonal rates require temporal aggregation, date parsing, and quantified peak/off-peak thresholds.
H2/H3 are contextual rather than compiled, and the special-attestation source and exact Standard/Complex rule are incomplete.
A public period-level approval metric exists, but H24 is unresolved and the HKB does not specify which period or how multiple periods map to an attorney.
Employer worksite spread inherits H27 aggregation and lacks a defined region taxonomy.
The dependency flag exists, but employer workforce proportions needed for the three levels are absent and require employer-grain aggregation.
H21 is unresolved, and many, limited, and very few candidates have no public thresholds or candidate-count source.
Average WDR must be joined or attributed from LCA wage rows to an employer and aggregated across applications.
H37 cannot produce the required complexity score, and the conversion from its unspecified weights to factor counts is undefined.
Distinct filing months per employer require parsed dates, a chosen year, and employer-level temporal aggregation.
The comparison requires two approval-rate populations and inherits unresolved global and attorney attribution semantics from H13 and H24.
OES presence and alternative source type are split across leaves, and Survey does not distinguish an independent published survey that meets DOL requirements.
